visual.general_description: A portrait document page titled CFT for Psychosis - Manual: a header with three institution logos and a list of researcher roles, a shaded Overview of therapy levels box, and a two-column table of therapy levels (Starting therapy, levels 1 to 5, Ending therapy) with numbered sub-items.
visual.detailed_description: Header: three institution logos at the top left and a right-aligned text block naming the lead researcher, therapist and author, the research supervisors and therapy collaborators. Title line reads CFT for Psychosis - Manual with a red note that the full 50-page CFTp manual is available from the first author on request. An Overview of therapy levels box states that the ordering of levels 1 to 5 guides the therapist, that therapy is process-driven, and that levels may be re-ordered, blended or skipped. Below, a bordered table lists: Starting therapy (S.1 to S.3); level 1 Establishing safeness and connection (1.1 external safeness, 1.2 internal safeness with sub-items); level 2 Learning about evolved (tricky) brains, emotional systems and multiple selves (2.1 to 2.4); level 3 Understanding how my emotions and mind have become shaped (3.1 to 3.4); level 4 Building the compassionate self (4.1 to 4.3 with sub-items); level 5 Directing compassion to self, others, emotional parts and voices (5.1, 5.2 with sub-items); Ending therapy (E.1 to E.3). Small up-down arrow symbols sit under each level number. The footer reads CFT for psychosis manual, Version 2, with a date and a research ethics committee reference.
